topic: Forces and Their Effects on Motion
key_concepts: A force is a push or pull.
Forces can make an object move, move faster, slow down, stop, or change direction.
Forces do not always cause motion.
Force is described by magnitude, direction, point of application, and line of action.
The SI unit of force is the newton; other units include dyne and pound.
Contact forces occur when objects touch and include applied force, friction, normal force,
Friction opposes motion, and air resistance is a frictional force.
Normal force acts perpendicular to the surface of contact.
Tension is a force applied through a string, rope, chain, or cable.
Non-contact forces act over a field and include gravitational and magnetic forces.
Gravitational force depends on the masses and distance between objects and causes weight.
